entries.answer:
1. [lines 48-70 / `parse_dragonfly_url`] — `parsed.port` (line 53) and `int(port_raw)` (lines 53, 60, 64) raise `ValueError` at module import time if `DRAGONFLY_URL` contains a non-numeric port or `DRAGONFLY_PORT` env var is non-numeric; only the `rsplit` branch is guarded.
2. [line 108 / `dragonfly_client = create_dragonfly_connection(...)`] — import-time network call blocks startup for up to 10s and requires `redis` reachable at import.
3. [line 115 / `class DragonflyStorage.TTL_SECONDS`] — Redis/Dragonfly `SETEX` maximum is 2^31-1 ms is fine, but key TTL of 365 days conflicts with `SESSION_TIMEOUT` (line 1447, also 365d) while `cleanup_old_sessions` deletes in-memory sessions on the same 365d TTL — sessions in Dragonfly and memory use different `created_at` semantics (memory cleanup never runs in practice, see #20).
4. [line 160 / `get_user_conversations`] — `client.smembers()` returns bytes when `decode_responses=True` client is reused after reconnect via `_get_client()` default... — `DragonflyStorage._get_client()` reconnects with `decode_responses=True` but conv_id byte decode handled; however `get_user_conversations` lacks the `# type: ignore` handling and mixes bytes/str — inconsistent with `get_user_research_sessions` (ambiguity).
5. [line 870 / `re.findall(r'(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)', line)`] — double backslash inside a raw string: the regex matches a literal backslash followed by one-or-more "d" letters instead of digits, so `extract_confidence_from_response` never finds any number and always returns 0.75.
6. [line 915 / `call_tiffy_api` default `max_tokens=250000`] — exceeds Grok API max output; every agent call (line 1311 passes 250000) and the report planner request a completion length the API will reject (HTTP 400).
7. [line 923 / `"stream": include_reasoning`] — payload sets `stream=True` whenever `include_reasoning=True`, but the non-streaming branch (line 948, taken when `session_id is None`, as in all ~13 feature calls) later deletes only `"reasoning"` from a copy; the copy sets `"stream": False` (line 949) — OK there, but the main `payload` retains `stream=True` when `include_reasoning=True and session_id` is falsy in the streaming branch condition on line 932 — the branch check requires both flags, so `include_reasoning=True` with `session_id=None` silently drops the requested `reasoning` field from the result.
8. [line 932 / `if include_reasoning and session_id`] — when `include_reasoning=True` but `session_id` is None (13 call sites, e.g. lines 2850, 2932, 3058, 3135, 3181, 3530, 3575, 3639, 3702, 3800, 3855, 3917), the returned dict has no `'reasoning'` key, but callers use `result.get('reasoning', '')` — reasoning content is silently never produced (logic error).
9. [line 946 / `tokens_used = chunk['usage'].get('total_tokens', 0)`] — in the streaming loop, `usage` typically only appears in the final chunk; if the stream ends at `[DONE]` before a usage chunk, `tokens_used` stays 0 — undercounting (logic).
10. [line 1004 / `call_grok4_api(... include_reasoning=False)`] — hard-codes `stream=False` payload for all expert agents, so 8 agents × 250000-token requests time out at the fixed 180s timeout (line 952) under load — runtime timeout not handled as retryable (see #11).
11. [line 990-996 / `call_tiffy_api` retry] — on generic `Exception` containing "429" the code `continue`s only if `attempt < max_retries - 1`; after the loop it raises `last_error`, but a `requests.Timeout` on the final attempt sets `last_error` then falls out of loop and raises — yet HTTP 4xx/5xx raised at line 946/957 inside the generic handler with non-429 text re-raises immediately (line 998 `raise`), skipping retries — inconsistent retry semantics.
12. [line 1311 / `run_single_expert_agent` → `call_grok4_api(... max_tokens=250000 ...)`] — duplicates error #6 (same limit bug at a second call site).
13. [line 1343 / `future.result(timeout=None)`] — no timeout on agent futures: one hung agent blocks the entire 8-agent group forever.
14. [line 1356-1405 / `compute_consensus`] — defined but never called anywhere (dead code).
15. [line 1407 / `run_meta_synthesis`] — defined but never called anywhere (dead code).
16. [line 1320 / `run_expert_group_parallel`] — defined but never called anywhere (dead code); the "8 expert agents" pipeline is unreachable.
17. [line 26 / `MAX_SSE_CLIENTS_PER_SESSION = 10`] — constant defined but never enforced; SSE clients are appended unbounded at line 2458.
18. [line 1446 / `SESSION_TIMEOUT = 365*24*3600`] — used by `cleanup_old_sessions` but `_last_cleanup` check (line 1451) returns early before acquiring the lock when interval hasn't elapsed — fine — but `CLEANUP_INTERVAL=3600` (line 1448) combined with 365-day timeout means cleanup effectively never deletes sessions (they live 1 year); also `RESEARCH_SESSIONS` has no max size — unbounded memory growth.
19. [line 1458 / `datetime.fromisoformat(s.created_at).timestamp()`] — raises `ValueError` if `created_at` is ever a malformed/naive-with-offset string (comes from `datetime.now().isoformat()`, naive — OK), but the same call will raise on any externally-restored session data — unhandled inside the cleanup loop aborts entire cleanup.
20. [line 1477 / `broadcast_sse_event` calls `cleanup_old_sessions()`] — and `cleanup_old_sessions` is also called by `before_request` (line 2582) and `health` (line 2560) — three trigger sites, none on a timer; cleanup only runs opportunistically.
21. [line 1728 / `run_autonomous_research` save] — `session_data` dict saved to Dragonfly contains key `'final_response'` but chat endpoints (lines 2068, 2141) read `latest_research.get('final_report')` — key mismatch: research context is always empty (broken reference between writer and readers).
22. [line 2068, 2141 / `latest_research.get('final_report')`] — see #21: key never written; also `user_research_sessions[0]` takes an arbitrary element of a Redis set order (SMEMBERS unordered), not the "latest" (logic error).
23. [line 1849 / `requests.post(... timeout=None)`] — OAuth token exchange has no timeout; a hung Kinde server blocks the worker thread indefinitely.
24. [line 1855 / `requests.get(... timeout=None)`] — user profile fetch has no timeout (same hang risk).
25. [line 1840 / `validate_oauth_state(state)` result ignored] — on mismatch the code only logs a warning and proceeds with token exchange, defeating CSRF protection (security/logic error).
26. [line 1858 / `session['user'] = {...}`] — `name` fallback `user_data.get('email', '').split('@')[0]` crashes with `AttributeError` if `email` is present but `None` (`None.split`) — `dict.get('email', '')` returns None when key exists with null value.
27. [line 2464 / `q.get(timeout=None)`] — SSE generator blocks forever waiting on the queue; the `except queue.Empty` heartbeat branch below it (lines 2466-2471) is unreachable code because `timeout=None` never raises `queue.Empty` — connection never heartbeats, never breaks on COMPLETED/FAILED.
28. [line 2470 / `session.status in [TaskStatus.COMPLETED, TaskStatus.FAILED]`] — even if reachable, `session` here is the `ResearchSession` object; comparison against Enum members is fine, but this code is dead due to #27.
29. [line 2539 / `delayed_research` thread `daemon=False`] — non-daemon thread spawned per research; server cannot shut down until research completes (hours); with `app.run(threaded=True)` this also leaks threads on errors before completion.
30. [line 881-883 / `sanitize_filename`] — duplicate of `secure_filename` (line 26) with different, weaker rules (allows leading dots and path chars after `..` removal like `%2e%2e`); two competing sanitizers is an ambiguity; `sanitize_filename` is used in `process_uploaded_file` (line 1994) while download path uses `secure_filename` (line 2516) — inconsistent.
31. [line 1994-2013 / `process_uploaded_file`] — `file.read()` loads the whole (up to 100MB) upload into memory just to measure size, then `file.seek(0)`; also `content = f.read()[:5000]` reads the entire file then slices — wasteful; more importantly for a 100MB binary file `open(...,'r',errors='ignore')` reads 100MB fully before slicing.
32. [line 2530 / `research_chat`] — `except PermissionError` (line 2427) can never be raised by any code in the try block — dead except clause; access-denied actually returns via `jsonify` inside the lock block.
33. [line 3088 / bare `except:`] — bare except in `semantic_research_map` swallows `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`.
34. [line 2858 / `"IGAZ" in content.upper() and "HAMIS" not in content.upper()`] — substring match: "HAMIS" appears inside words like "HAMISÍTÁS", "NEM HAMIS", and "RÉSZBEN IGAZ" contains "IGAZ" — the verdict classifier misclassifies "RÉSZBEN IGAZ" as "IGAZ" when "HAMIS" absent (checks IGAZ before RÉSZBEN), and any text containing "HAMIS" anywhere flips a true verdict to HAMIS (logic error).
35. [line 3249 / `replace('{', '\\\\{')`] — inside the file this is `'\\{'` written with doubled backslashes in a non-raw string, i.e. replacement text is `\\{` (two chars: backslash+backslash+brace → actually `\` + `\{`); BibTeX escaping doubles the backslash, producing invalid BibTeX output `\\{`.
36. [line 882 / `replace('\\\\', '')`] — non-raw string with four backslashes = two literal backslashes; only removes double-backslash sequences, leaving single `\` in filenames intact — path separator on Windows not stripped (sanitizer incomplete).
37. [line 243 / `# type: ignore` comments on `smembers`] — multiple `# type: ignore[arg-type]` / `[union-attr]` suppressions (lines 203, 236-239, 1343) indicate known type errors being silenced rather than fixed (type errors).
38. [line 12 / `from cerebras.cloud.sdk import Cerebras`] — third-party import with no fallback: `ModuleNotFoundError` at startup if `cerebras-cloud-sdk` not installed; same class of hard failure for `flask_session` (line 15), `sklearn` (line 9), `redis` (line 11).
39. [line 1066 / `call_cerebras_chat` model `"gpt-oss-120b"`] — and `stream_cerebras_chat` (line 1096) same model; if the model name is not available on the account every chat call raises — unvalidated external dependency (ambiguity/broken reference risk).
40. [line 2581-2583 / `before_request` sets `session.permanent = True`] — mutates Flask session on every request including static files; combined with `Session(app)` redis backend this forces a session cookie/write for every request (performance/logic).
41. [line 1442 / `CONVERSATIONS = {}` and `RESEARCH_SESSIONS = {}` and `SSE_CLIENTS = {}`] — module-level in-memory stores duplicated against Dragonfly persistence; on multi-worker deployment the two stores diverge (architectural logic error; reads fall back to the local dict only on the same process).
42. [line 1737 / `session.final_response = final_report[:10000]`] — full report truncated to 10k chars for the "final_response" while the UI/SSE event (line 1744) truncates to 5000 — two different truncation sizes for the same content (ambiguity).
43. [line 1613 / `tiffy_create_report_outline` fallback] — fallback returns sections with `"key_points": []`, but `write_report_segment_with_gptoss` line 1587 does `chr(10).join(section.get('key_points', [...]))` — when key_points exists but is an empty list the join produces an empty string and the "FŐ PONTOK" block is blank (logic), and when key_points contains non-strings, `chr(10).join` raises TypeError.
44. [line 1453 / `re.search(r'\{[^{}]*"queries"[^{}]*\}', content, re.DOTALL)`] — regex `[^{}]*` forbids nested braces, so any JSON with nested objects fails to match and silently falls back to the default plan (logic error in plan parsing).
45. [line 2360 / `re.search(r'\[[\s\S]*\]', content)`] — greedy `[\s\S]*` across the whole content grabs from the first `[` to the last `]`, including non-JSON prose containing brackets — `json.loads` then raises and hits the generic fallback (logic).
46. [line 2960 / `re.search(r'\{[\s\S]*\}', content)`] — same greedy-brace problem in `build_knowledge_graph` (grabs too much, `json.loads` fails, graph returned empty).
47. [line 1667 / `progress = 55 + (i / len(report_outline)) * 35`] — `ZeroDivisionError` if `report_outline` is an empty list (possible when `sections` is empty); guarded only implicitly by the for loop not executing — but the loop not executing also means no report segments are ever written and the "report" is empty while status still becomes COMPLETED (logic).
48. [line 1700-1702 / report file write] — `open(report_path, 'w')` writes into `UPLOAD_FOLDER` without checking disk space/permissions; exception is caught by outer handler but `session.final_report_path` remains None silently — status still COMPLETED on partial failure path? — actually exception propagates to outer except → FAILED; but `report_size` computed after write; fine — real issue: `final_report_path` stores a server-local path that is later re-`secure_filename`-sanitized at download (line 2516) — `secure_filename` strips nothing from an already-safe name, OK — but `download_research_report` reconstructs path from `UPLOAD_FOLDER + secure_filename(basename(...))`, so a report written to a different directory would 404 (ambiguity).
49. [line 2585-2612 / `calculate_source_quality`] — `peer_reviewed=True` is set for `.edu`/`.gov` domains (line 2677) which are not peer-reviewed sources (logic error); `citation_count` counts word occurrences of "citation"/"et al" in text, not real citations (misleading metric).
50. [line 2712 / `authenticity_score = 70` starting value] — heuristic returns an "authenticity_score" with arbitrary constants (−30/−20) and a `call_tiffy_findsimilar` result listed as "similar_sources" presented as verification — simulated/placeholder verification logic (fake authenticity check).
51. [line 848 / `generate_simple_embedding`] — MD5-hash-based pseudo-"embedding" is a simulated/fake semantic embedding: `compute_consensus` clustering on it (line 1373) produces meaningless clusters (placeholder content presented as real semantics).
52. [line 3052-3089 / `semantic_research_map`] — `depth` parameter only checks `depth > 1` and iterates `subtopics[:5]` regardless of actual depth value; `depth=3` behaves identically to `depth=2` (parameter ignored — logic error).
53. [line 4718 / `app.run(..., debug=os.environ.get('DEBUG','False').lower() == 'true', threaded=True)`] — hardcoded `host='0.0.0.0', port=5000` ignores env configuration; debug mode can be enabled via env in production, exposing the Werkzeug debugger (security/logic).
54. [line 2458 / `SSE_CLIENTS[session_id].append(q)`] — unbounded growth; `MAX_SSE_CLIENTS_PER_SESSION` never enforced (duplicate of #17 merged — keeping once).
55. [line 2558 / `health()` calls `cleanup_old_sessions()`] — plus `before_request` (line 2582) — every request runs the cleanup check; with `_last_cleanup` gate it's cheap, but the 1-year timeout (line 1446) makes it a no-op — cleanup subsystem effectively non-functional (logic).
56. [line 4713-4718 / startup logs "Advanced features loaded: 50 cutting-edge capabilities"] — hardcoded marketing string claims 50 capabilities; actual implemented feature functions ≈ 20 (fabricated/placeholder status message).
57. [line 1007 / `call_exa_search` wrapper], [line 1051 `call_exa_contents`], [line 1080 `call_exa_findsimilar`], [line 1111 `call_exa_answer`] — `call_exa_answer` and `call_exa_contents` are never called anywhere (dead code).
58. [line 476-500 / `add_chat_memory`] — spawns a daemon thread per chat message (lines 2190, 2269) hitting the SuperMemory API with no rate limiting; failures in the thread are unlogged/unhandled (thread target exceptions print to stderr only).
59. [line 2206 / `threading.Thread(target=SuperMemoryClient.add_chat_memory, ...)`] — the thread races with the response return; if the process exits, memory write is silently lost (daemon thread) — reliability logic error.
60. [line 2446, 2469 / `session = RESEARCH_SESSIONS.get(session_id)`] — local variable `session` shadows Flask's imported `session` within `research_chat`, `research_events`, `get_research_status`, `download_research_report`; in `research_events` the shadow happens inside the generator while `get_current_user()` (which uses Flask `session`) is called before — works by luck of ordering; in `before_request` (line 2583) `session.permanent = True` still refers to Flask session — ambiguity hazard: any later edit adding a Flask-session access after the shadow breaks silently.

END OF ERROR LIST.
